Hi Emma — great to connect. Attached is an initial MAP and a concise GPU sizing recommendation tailored to the pilot. High level summary below; full details in the attached MAP_v2.xlsx and a quick diagram (gpu-sizing-diagram.png).

Summary recommendations (short):
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): typical provisioning lead time 4–6 weeks from signed commitment; supports fast ramping, predictable unit economics, and isolated pools.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): 8–12 weeks end-to-end (networking, KMS, security review); useful if you need air-gapped or strict data residency.
- Suggested pilot pool (baseline + burst): 2 x A100-80GB nodes (baseline), autoscale to 4–6 nodes for peak. That maps to roughly ~12–20 GPU-hours/hour at peak depending on batching/sequence length.
- Canary & eval plan: 2-week internal canary (10% of traffic) → 4-week external pilot with weekly quality checkpoints. Gate to full rollout: latency p99 < 800ms, error rate < 0.5%, and cost/unit within agreed threshold.

Next steps (what I need from you):
1) Confirm pilot start window (you mentioned mid-July) and decision deadline.
2) Share a sample prompt set (10–20 prompts) for quality gating.
3) Confirm whether you prefer Dedicated first or Private evaluation.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (mutual action plan), gpu-sizing-diagram.png (high-level topology). I will follow up with a short SOW draft and a HubSpot link to the deal.

Emma / Soojin — quick technical addendum on sizing and eval metrics from SE side. Key points:

- Model assumptions: LLaMA-variant, FP16, 8k context; peak per-request tokens ~ 400 (in/out).
- Mem footprint: ~60–70GB VRAM for model + KV cache for 8k context; A100-80GB recommended to avoid spilling.

Sizing math (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline throughput target: 10 qps × avg 400 tokens/request × 1 token generation cost ~ 0.003s on A100 (approx) = ~12 token-seconds/sec => well within 2 GPUs with batching of 8–16.
- Peak (30 qps): require sustained batching + autoscale to 4 GPUs; for bursty traffic recommend quicker auto-burst policy to 6 GPUs for short windows.

Operational notes:
- Continuous batching with 100ms latency target reduces GPU-hours by ~35% vs no-batching.
- KV cache warm starts: plan for a warm-up window (canary) of 24–48 hours where we pre-populate frequent prefixes; MAP should include that as a milestone.

Delivery timelines:
- Dedicated: infra-prep + pool provisioning = 3–4 weeks after PO if we re-use standard instance types in our hosted/DC partners; 4–6 weeks for reserved contract and capacity guarantees.
- Private (VPC): 8–12 weeks inclusive of security reviews and customer infra changes.

If you want, I can produce a short performance runbook and a rough cost model for the pilot (tokens, GPU-hours).

—Karthik

Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
